subject: Quick sync: pilot fit + ramp estimates for clinical notes summarization
messages:
From: Eli Monroe <eli@arborhealth.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Interested in a demo — evaluation for clinical notes summarization

Hi Sofia,

We just signed up for the self-serve sandbox and I'm interested in a short demo to understand how Redwood could help with automatic clinical notes summarization and de-identification for our telehealth platform.

A few quick context points:
- Use case: summarize clinician-patient visit notes, redact PHI before export, and surface short action items for care coordinators.
- Volume: ~120k notes / month initially, average note ~600 words; peak concurrent users ~20 during U.S. business hours.
- Timeline: aim to pilot in 6–8 weeks, production by end of Q2 if pilot looks good.
- Requirements: PHI handling / SOC2 / potential BAAs — we can discuss.

I attached a small CSV with a redacted sample note and a schema (sample-data-schema.csv). Could we run a 30–40 minute walkthrough next week? I'm on PST.

Thanks,
Eli Monroe
Director of Data Engineering
Arbor Health
eli@arborhealth.com

---
Attachment: sample-data-schema.csv (CSV, 2 KB)
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Eli Monroe <eli@arborhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Interested in a demo — evaluation for clinical notes summarization

Hi Eli — great to meet you and thanks for the context + sample. I'm Sofia on the SDR team at Redwood — happy to run the intro and loop in Ben (solutions engineering) for the technical portion.

Before we lock a slot, two quick qualification items so Ben can prep targeted examples:
1) Latency & throughput expectations: is sub-second token latency required for the live path, or is near-real-time (1–3s/token) acceptable for batch summarization?
2) Redaction needs: do you need deterministic PHI redaction on ingest (blocklist + regex) or are you expecting post-generation redaction/validation steps?
3) Integration target: are you planning to call the API from a backend service or run a private deployment (VPC / on-prem) for PHI?
4) Pilot success metrics: what pilot KPIs would make you move to prod (accuracy threshold, cost per note, throughput)?

Proposed slots (30–40m) next week (PST):
- Wed 2/16 10:00–10:40 AM PST
- Wed 2/16 2:00–2:40 PM PST
- Thu 2/17 11:00–11:40 AM PST

If none of those work, tell me your preferred windows and we can reschedule. I attached a short "pre-demo checklist" you can skim — includes example questions and what to bring (pre-demo-checklist.pdf).

Thanks — I'll confirm once I hear your answers and preferred slot.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
SDR, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0183

Attachment: pre-demo-checklist.pdf (PDF, 75 KB)
From: Eli Monroe <eli@arborhealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 08:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Interested in a demo — evaluation for clinical notes summarization

Hi Sofia — thanks for the quick reply and the checklist, that's helpful. Answers below: 

1) Latency: for the initial pilot we only need near-real-time/batch (1–3s per 300 tokens) for nightly processing; live UI features are a later phase.
2) Redaction: we need deterministic redaction on ingest for exported notes (names, MRNs, dates). Post-generation validation is fine as an additional check.
3) Integration: we'll start with API calls from a backend service (hosted in AWS us-west-2). We'll evaluate Private options if BAAs/PHI require it.
4) Pilot KPIs: 85%+ accuracy on extracted action items, under $0.10 / note processing cost (target), and throughput ~5k notes/hour during validation runs.

Wed 2/16 2:00–2:40 PM PST works for our team — can you confirm and send a calendar invite? Also, do you have a short architecture primer or runbook we can read ahead of the call?

Eli
